'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[2022 missile explosion in Poland]]
****A missile strike kills two people in the village of [[Przewodów]] in eastern [[Poland]]. [[President of the United States]] [[Joe Biden]] says that the missile blast in Poland was caused by a Ukrainian air defense missile. U.S. officials had earlier told the [[Associated Press]] that preliminary findings suggested that the missile that hit Poland was fired by [[Ukrainian forces]] at an incoming Russian missile. [https://www.reuters.com/article/ukraine-crisis-poland-blast-missiles/poland-blast-caused-by-missile-fired-by-ukrainian-forces-at-incoming-russian-missile-ap-idUSKBN2S60AQ (Reuters)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/biden-said-ukraine-air-defence-missile-responsible-poland-blast-nato-source-2022-11-16/ (Reuters 2)]
****The [[Polish Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] says that it was a "Russian-made missile" and summons the Russian [[ambassador]] to provide an explanation. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraine-hails-chinas-opposition-nuclear-threats-2022-11-15/ (Reuters)] [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-war-zelenskyy-kherson-9202c032cf3a5c22761ee71b52ff9d52 (AP)]
***[[November 2022 nationwide missile strikes on Ukraine]]
****Russian missiles strike several cities across [[Ukraine]], including [[Kyiv]], causing "critical" damage to energy facilities. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/nov/15/russia-launches-new-wave-of-missile-strikes-across-ukraine (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**[[November 2022 Ariel attack]]
***Three [[Israel]]is are killed and three others are injured after a 18-year-old [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] man carries out a [[vehicle-ramming attack]] and [[mass stabbing]] in the [[Ariel (settlement)|Ariel]] [[Israeli settlement|settlement]] in the occupied [[West Bank]]. The perpetrator is shot dead. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/3-seriously-wounded-in-stabbing-at-west-bank-industrial-zone-attacker-shot/ (''Times of Israel'')]
**The United States opens an investigation into the death of journalist [[Shireen Abu Akleh]], who was killed in the West Bank in May. [https://www.telam.com.ar/notas/202211/610925-cisjordania-periodista-asesinato-investigacion.html/ (Télam)]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**[[Foreign involvement in the Yemeni Civil War]]
***The [[US Navy]] says that it stopped an [[Iran]]ian shipment of 70 tons of missile fuel components and fertilizer to [[Yemen]]. The shipment would likely be used by the [[Houthis]], who are Iran's allies. [https://apnews.com/article/iran-united-states-dubai-arab-emirates-saudi-arabia-6e8c6bf72b9304c5bfcc3196478b2ecd (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2022 south eastern Australia floods]]
**[[Flood]]ing continues in [[Australia]], with over 220 people being rescued from floodwaters in [[New South Wales]] in the past 24 hours. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2022-11-15/nsw-floods-forbes-evacuation-wyangala-dam-newell-highway/101653738 (ABC News Australia)]
*At least three people are killed and six others are injured after a multi-storey building collapses in [[Nairobi]], [[Kenya]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/building-collapses-in-kenyas-capital-killing-three-people/2022/11/16/5cf6166e-65ba-11ed-b08c-3ce222607059_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*Fourteen people are killed after a minibus and a truck collide in [[Abu Minqar]], [[New Valley Governorate]], [[Egypt]]. [https://apnews.com/article/middle-east-africa-egypt-accidents-north-9546d21eb67a72f04bc1e60509f96629 (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Day of Eight Billion]]
**The [[world population]] [[world population milestones|surpasses]] eight billion people, according to the [[United Nations]]. [https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/the-world-population-passes-8-billion-today-how-big-will-it-get-mhqgz5vcw (''The Times'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[2022 G20 Bali summit]]
**The [[G20|Group of Twenty]] begins its annual two-day summit in [[Nusa Dua]], [[Bali]], [[Indonesia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/g20-summit-latest-biden-xi-meet-2022-11-14/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Mahsa Amini protests]]
**Protests are held across [[Iran]] to mark the third anniversary of the [[2019–2020 Iranian protests|2019 protests]]. Protesters blocked streets and a large strike has been reported. [https://www.iranintl.com/en/202211152390 (Iran International)]
*[[2024 Republican Party presidential primaries]]
**Former [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] announces [[Donald Trump 2024 presidential campaign|he is running]] for the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]]'s nomination in the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 U.S. presidential election]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2022/11/15/politics/trump-2024-presidential-bid/index.html (CNN)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2022 ATP Tour]]
**At 19 years old, Spanish [[tennis]] player [[Carlos Alcaraz]] becomes the youngest [[List of ATP number 1 ranked singles tennis players#Year-end No. 1 players|year-end world No. 1]]-[[ATP rankings|ranked]] [[Singles tennis|singles player]] by the [[Association of Tennis Professionals]] after his closest rival, fellow Spaniard [[Rafael Nadal]], failed to advance to the semifinals of the [[2022 ATP Finals – Singles|2022 ATP Finals]]. Alcaraz breaks Australian player [[Lleyton Hewitt]]'s record that he achieved in 2001. [https://www.couriermail.com.au/sport/tennis/carlos-alcaraz-crushes-lleyton-hewitt-record-to-become-youngest-yearend-world-no-1/news-story/3dca96e695112ec22800095d4f323b35 (''The Courier-Mail'')]
